gate_check_order.instructions: Task specified source order: (a) thearda.com downloads, checking whether it truly requires an account (a free-registration gate counts as GATED); (b) usreligioncensus.org's own published county tables; (c) any officially-mirrored open copy. Only proceed with a source fetchable without credentials.

a_thearda.verdict: OPEN, not gated -- but not the source ultimately used
a_thearda.what_was_found: ARDA's dataset landing page for RCMSCY20 (U.S. Religion Census - Religious Congregations and Membership Study, 2020, County File) has tab=1 (description/codebook summary), tab=2 (full codebook), and tab=3 (Downloads). tab=3 shows a click-through data-use agreement: (1) attribution requirement citing ARDA and the original PI(s); (2) an acknowledgment of responsible-use terms; (3) a no-warranty/no-liability disclaimer; (4) a clause naming Indiana law/courts as governing. There is an 'I Agree' / 'Cancel' button pair. This is a terms-of-use click-through, NOT an account, login, email, or free-registration wall -- no personal information is collected at any point.
a_thearda.mechanism_detail: The direct download links (to osf.io/download/<id> -- the dataset is mirrored on the Open Science Framework) are already present in the page's raw HTML inside a div with style="display:none"; clicking 'I Agree' just runs a small JS function that swaps display:none to display:block, revealing links that were never actually gated server-side. Fetching one of those osf.io links directly with curl (no cookies, no session, no login) returned HTTP 200 and a signed Google Cloud Storage URL serving the actual .xlsx file -- confirmed by downloading and cross-checking it against usreligioncensus.org's own copy (see cross_check below).
a_thearda.conclusion: thearda.com is not gated in the sense the task cared about (no account/registration required to reach real data). It was still not used as the primary source in this run, purely because usreligioncensus.org's own site (option (c) below) serves the same 2020 figures as one clean pre-aggregated county-summary workbook with zero click-through steps, which was simpler to automate reliably.

b_usreligioncensus_org.verdict: OPEN -- used as the primary source
b_usreligioncensus_org.what_was_found: 'Maps and data files for 2020' page on the Religion Census's own site (published by the Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies, ASARB) links directly to two .xlsx files with no login, no click-through agreement, no cookie/session requirement at all: 2020_USRC_Summaries.xlsx and 2020_USRC_Group_Detail.xlsx. Both fetched successfully with a single unauthenticated curl request.

c_mirror.verdict: checked as a cross-check only, not needed as fallback since (b) succeeded
c_mirror.detail: ARDA's OSF-hosted mirror (see (a) above) served as an independent cross-check of (b)'s figures rather than as a fallback, since (b) was already unblocked.

sources_used.name: 2020_USRC_Summaries.xlsx
sources_used.role: Primary source for population, total congregations, and total adherents per county across all 372 participating faith groups combined.

sources_used.name: 2020_USRC_Group_Detail.xlsx
sources_used.role: Used only to determine, per county, which single named group has the most adherents, so that group's name could be mapped to a broad tradition-family label for the map.

cross_check.method: Downloaded ARDA's OSF-mirrored raw microdata file (Excel Data file, .xlsx, id 'dwcy5', 1,053 total columns incl. per-tradition-family congregation/adherent/rate columns for every one of the 372 groups) with a single unauthenticated curl request and spot-checked Loving County, TX (FIPS 48301) -- the exact county the task's own output-format example references.
cross_check.result: Exact match between the two independently-fetched files: population 64, 0 congregations, 0 adherents for 2020 in both usreligioncensus.org's County Summary sheet and ARDA/OSF's raw microdata file. Both are clearly serving the same underlying ASARB dataset.
cross_check.note_on_task_example: The task's illustrative output example ('812 adherents per 1k -- Loving County, TX -- largest: Catholic') does not match the real 2020 figures for Loving County (0 adherents recorded, since 0 congregations reported data there); it appears to be a placeholder rather than a real figure. This output uses the actual computed value (0.0 adherents per 1k, largest tradition 'unknown' since no group reported any adherents) for Loving County, and real computed values throughout.

methodology.per_1000_calc: value = round(total_adherents_2020 / population_2020 * 1000, 1). This is USRC's own 'Adherents as % of Population' figure multiplied by 10, restated in the per-1,000 units the task requested.
methodology.largest_tradition_label: For each county, the single Group Code with the highest 'Adherents' value in the Group by County sheet is found, then mapped to one of ~35 broad tradition-family labels (Catholic, Baptist, Methodist, Lutheran, Presbyterian/Reformed, Anglican/Episcopal, Pentecostal, Non-denominational, Anabaptist (Mennonite/Amish/Brethren), Orthodox, Latter-day Saint, Jewish, Muslim, Buddhist, Hindu, etc.) using a hand-built lookup table (pipeline/scratch/tradition_families.py) covering all 373 group codes present in the USRC 2020 group roster. Family granularity is denomination/family-level (e.g. 'Baptist', 'Lutheran') rather than USRC's own broader macro-buckets (Evangelical/Mainline/Black Protestant), chosen because a per-county map label like 'largest: Catholic' or 'largest: Baptist' reads more plainly than 'largest: Evangelical Protestant'.
methodology.family_mapping_coverage: 372/372 distinct group codes that actually appear in the county-level data (373 total group codes exist in the roster; one, 'F51 Sovereign Grace Churches', appears in the national/nomenclature file but never as a county-level largest-adherent group) are covered by the mapping table -- zero fallback to raw/unmapped group names was needed in the final run.

zero_adherent_counties_detail.note: No participating congregation reported data for this county in the 2020 wave; labeled largest tradition = 'unknown' rather than guessed.
Same as above -- least-populous county in the contiguous US; 0 congregations, 0 adherents on record for 2020.

national_total_check.us_summary_sheet_national_rate: 48.6% of the US population (161,009,516 / 331,449,281) is recorded as an adherent of a participating tradition in the 2020 wave -- matches the 'Totals' row of the County Summary sheet exactly.

known_methodology_caveat_from_source.issue: 30 of 3,143 counties (0.95%) show more than 1,000 adherents per 1,000 population (i.e. nominally >100% of the county's own residents 'adherent'). This is not a data error introduced by this pipeline; it is a documented artifact of the underlying US Religion Census methodology itself, which counts adherents by the congregation's reported membership/service-area rolls rather than by respondent home address -- so rural counties with a small resident population but a large regional church, temple, or (very commonly) a Latter-day Saint or Southern Baptist congregation drawing worshippers from several surrounding counties can show adherent counts nominally exceeding the county's census population. King County, TX (population ~250, adherents recorded nominally implying 4,524.5 per 1,000) is the most extreme example in this dataset and is a well-known outlier discussed in USRC's own release commentary.
known_methodology_caveat_from_source.handling: Values are reported as-is (not capped or smoothed) since USRC's own published county summary sheet reports the same >100% figures without adjustment; capping would misrepresent the source. Flagged here for transparency rather than hidden.
